detail.longDescription: arXiv:2610.34548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: What does a recursive definition mean in a grounded logic, where a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? This paper takes Kripke's answer for truth, the least fixed point, as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term; Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, making each an inductive definition. IGA is omega-sound and proof-grounded: sound and complete for a semantics whose certificates are its own proofs. IGA proves Goodstein's theorem, the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, and, along Gentzen's route, the consistency of Peano Arithmetic. IGA certifies the Veblen notation below every $\varphi(n,0)$: its accessibility ordinal there is $\varphi(\omega,0)$, that of the paracomplete truth theory PKF. Every theorem is machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL; order types and PKF's ordinal are cited. IGA proves the Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for it, which it does not, and that bivalence is sound exactly when the order is well-founded. So $\Gamma_0$ lies exactly one instance of excluded middle away, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in an internal form of Kleene's $\mathcal{O}$ are interderivable over IGA. Bivalence at the Bachmann-Howard order keeps proof-groundedness. One such claim buys well-foundedness of the countable part of Buchholz's notation at every finite level, of type $\psi_0(\Omega_\omega)$, and $k$ stratified bivalence rules give a proof-grounded system proving the countable part up to level $k$ well-founded; $k$ iterated closings-off of truth do too, sound only for a closed-off model. Unrestricted conditional proof is inconsistent (Curry's paradox); the purchase is implication at a hypothesis not provably decided.
